stemBlocks.value: Quadrilateral R has vertices (1, 1), (4, 1), (4, 4) and (1, 2); its image S has vertices (-1, -5), (5, -5), (5, 1) and (-1, -3). Describe fully the single transformation that maps R onto S.
Think first: S is clearly bigger than R but the same shape, so this is an enlargement and the work is to find the scale factor and the centre.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p264-q11 from workbook page 264.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the vertices of R and S and pair them up.
Compare the length of one side of R with the matching side of S.

contentBlocks.value: The base of R runs from (1, 1) to (4, 1), a length of 3; the base of S runs from (-1, -5) to (5, -5), a length of 6.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the centre C using image = 2 x object - C, so C = 2 x object - image.
Confirm the centre with a second pair of vertices.

contentBlocks.value: Using (4, 4) -> (5, 1):  C = (2(4) - 5, 2(4) - 1) = (3, 7). The other two pairs give the same point.
Positive scale factor, so the image is on the same side of the centre as the object and the same way up.

strategyBlocks.value: Compare a pair of corresponding side lengths to get the scale factor, then use the rule image = k x object - (k - 1) x centre, or join corresponding vertices with straight lines and find where they meet.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: An enlargement with centre (3, 7) and scale factor 2.

whyThisWorks.value: An enlargement multiplies the displacement of every point from a fixed centre by the same scale factor, so all lengths are multiplied by k while all angles are unchanged. That is why the image is similar to the object, and why the vector equation image - centre = k(object - centre) rearranges to centre = (k x object - image)/(k - 1); with k = 2 this simplifies to centre = 2 x object - image. Any two corresponding pairs must give the same centre, which is a built-in check.

commonErrors.misconception: Giving the scale factor as the ratio of areas (4) instead of the ratio of lengths (2).
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Giving the scale factor as the ratio of areas (4) instead of the ratio of lengths (2).

commonErrors.misconception: Describing it as 'enlargement scale factor 2' with no centre, which is not a full description.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Describing it as 'enlargement scale factor 2' with no centre, which is not a full description.

examTip.value: To locate a centre of enlargement quickly, draw straight lines through two pairs of corresponding vertices and extend them until they cross; the crossing point is the centre.
